title: K-12 District Website and Board Portal Platforms (50,000+ served) | SignalFeed.dev
description: Which website platforms and board-meeting portals US school districts serving 50,000+ people use, for 1,322 district websites, ahead of the April 2027 ADA Title II date.
h1: K-12 district platforms: websites and board portals of districts serving 50,000+
body:
School districts serving 50,000 or more people reach the ADA Title II web rule's compliance date on April 26, 2027: web content, including the PDFs on board-meeting portals, must conform to WCAG 2.1 Level AA, subject to the rule's exceptions. Which platforms do those districts' websites and board documents run on? We checked 1,442 districts serving 50,000+ people (Census SAIPE 2024 estimates, websites from NCES).

Website platforms

Website platform of the 1,322 districts with a website on file, identified for 967 of them, mostly from public DNS records (no site visit needed) and otherwise from homepage markup. Platforms seen on fewer than two districts are omitted.

Why it matters for Title II

Board packets, policies and minutes on a separate portal are still the district's web content. A district's accessibility work has to cover the portal's PDFs too, and website-only audits miss them.

What this is, and what it isn't

These are observations of public records and pages: a website platform appears because the site's DNS points to it or its markup shows it; a board portal appears because the district's site links to it. They are not vendor-confirmed customer lists, and board-portal counts cover only districts we could visit. Population is a Census estimate, so districts near 50,000 should confirm which compliance date applies.
